key_insight: Tiering is free and proven (Meta TMO saves 20-32% of memory), but enterprise fleets skip it for risk and effort. Payment from avoided DRAM buys at 4x prices aligns incentives.
killer_doubt: Savings are counterfactual: purchases are avoided only at 4-6-year refresh, so the baseline is gameable. VMware already compresses memory; adopters may save ~10-20%, only ~2-4% of world bits.
decisive_experiment: Pilot on 200-500 servers at 3-5 enterprise customers (~$400k): profile cold pages at a 2-minute threshold, enable zswap or CXL tiering, track resident-memory cut and p99 latency for 6 months, and trial an IPMVP-style baseline.
prior_art: Meta TMO (ASPLOS'22); Google zswap far memory (ASPLOS'19); MemVerge, Kove software tiers; VMware memory compression. Shared-savings memory contracts: none found.

key_insight: Pricing per effective GB pushes compression into the memory controller, where it is cheapest; random-access line compression gives ~1.5-2x on general server data.
killer_doubt: Dedup across 1,000 hosts cannot be load/store: multi-hop CXL lookups add ~0.5-1 us. BF16 weights compress only ~1.3x and accelerator weights sit in HBM, so 10x falls to ~2x.
decisive_experiment: FPGA CXL Type-3 prototype (~$200k) with LZ4-class line compression and a hash-dedup table; replay host-memory snapshots from 20 inference and 20 general servers; measure effective capacity ratio and added load latency.
prior_art: IBM MXT compressed main memory (2001); ZeroPoint CXL compression IP; HICAMP (ASPLOS 2012); Linux KSM. From memory.

key_insight: OMI and FB-DIMM died of single-vendor lock-in, not physics; an open generation-agnostic CXL buffer with ECC and patrol scrub is the right way to manage aged parts.
killer_doubt: Already shipping as commercial CXL-DDR4 controllers. DDR3 adds 4 Gb dies at a third of DDR4 bandwidth, not worth a PHY. Retiring server DRAM is ~6-10% of bit demand.
decisive_experiment: Buy a commercial CXL-DDR4 card (~$20k), fill it with 5-7-year-old RDIMMs, and log 30 days of corrected errors, retention and row-hammer events under production traces; nothing new needs building.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024) reuses DDR4 behind CXL; Marvell Structera X and Astera Leo CXL controllers support DDR4 (from memory).

key_insight: One chipkill-protected, telemetry-driven controller over DDR3, DDR4 and LPDDR4 is the right abstraction; the LPDDR4 port reaches phone-scrap supply that DIMM reuse cannot.
killer_doubt: Chipkill needs lockstep devices of one width, so mixed vintages get per-rank ECC only. DDR4 already ships behind commercial CXL cards; a 28 nm tapeout plus PHY IP costs ~$2-5M.
decisive_experiment: FPGA CXL prototype (~$150k) driving retired DDR4 RDIMMs plus reballed phone LPDDR4 on adapter boards: measure per-rank ECC overhead, mixed-rank bandwidth and corrected-error rates over 90 days.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024) reuses DDR4 behind CXL; Marvell Structera X and Astera Leo CXL controllers support DDR4 (from memory).

key_insight: Retired DDR4 is zero-capex supply during a ~4x price spike; DRAM barely wears out, so 5-year-old DIMMs keep most of their life.
killer_doubt: Already deployed at hyperscale. Behind CXL it adds ~70-150 ns, so it serves cold pages (~20-30% of footprint); retirement volume (~6-10% of bit demand) cannot cover 20-30% of new capacity.
decisive_experiment: No feasibility test needed; a ~$50k census of retiring DDR4 GB against new-server cold-tier demand settles the realistic supply share.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024) reuses DDR4 behind CXL; Marvell Structera X and Astera Leo CXL controllers support DDR4 (from memory).

key_insight: CXL 3.x shared memory lets one physical copy of read-only data (weights, images, libraries) serve many hosts; explicit sharing gets this without hashing every page.
killer_doubt: Weights live in accelerator HBM, and tensor-parallel shards store them once per group, so AI dedup ratio is ~1. Hash indirection adds ~50-100 ns per miss; KSM-class gains are 1.1-1.5x.
decisive_experiment: Snapshot host DRAM of 32 inference and 32 general servers in one rack (~$100k); count rack-wide versus per-host duplicate 4 KB pages, separating file-backed pages that one shared DAX mapping already covers.
prior_art: HICAMP (ASPLOS 2012); Linux KSM; VMware TPS; CXL 3.0 memory sharing; vLLM prefix caching; Phase B B4 notes rejected AI-tensor dedup.

key_insight: Prices can reveal which jobs value marginal GBs most, so a pool can lend idle DRAM without central forecasts of each host's demand.
killer_doubt: Pond-style pooling saves only ~7-9% of DRAM. Reclaiming 1 GB over CXL takes ~30 ms plus TLB shootdowns, and allocations live minutes to hours, so millisecond leases add nothing.
decisive_experiment: Trace-driven simulation (~$50k) on public Azure and Google cluster memory traces: compare auction allocation with Pond-style ML placement for DRAM saved and SLA violations.
prior_art: Microsoft Pond CXL pooling (ASPLOS'23); Ginseng market-driven memory allocation (VEE 2014); Resource-as-a-Service cloud proposals. From memory.

key_insight: Running aged DDR4 below rated speed buys timing margin, a cheap way to tolerate drifted parts behind CXL.
killer_doubt: Duplicate of deployed DDR4-behind-CXL reuse. DRAM wear-out at rated speed is negligible, so slowing it adds margin, not life. Supply ceiling ~6-10% of bit demand.
decisive_experiment: No device test needed; the same ~$50k retirement-volume census as I-08711 bounds how much new DDR5 this displaces.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024) reuses DDR4 behind CXL; Marvell Structera X and Astera Leo CXL controllers support DDR4 (from memory).

key_insight: Buyer distrust of used DIMMs is real friction; a host-written lifetime log (hours, temperature, corrected errors, hammer events) holds grading data that one-shot bench tests miss.
killer_doubt: SPD is a copyable ~1 KB EEPROM (~1e5-1e6 writes): a BMC-signed log can be cloned onto a worse DIMM unless bound to a die fingerprint such as its retention-failure map.
decisive_experiment: Firmware pilot (~$150k): BMCs write signed logs to 1,000 DIMMs for a year; test whether logs predict post-retirement retention and error rates, and try cloning against a retention-map binding.
prior_art: BMC and Redfish memory error logs; DDR5 SPD hub thermal sensor; Blancco-style ITAD certificates; stage-2 HOLD I-08260 (retention-map certificate).

key_insight: Room-temperature DRAM remanence lasts seconds to minutes, so a DIMM unpowered for an hour holds no recoverable data; shredding DIMMs has no physical basis.
killer_doubt: Guidance exists: manuals citing NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 1 treat DRAM as volatile, sanitized by power removal and a 5-10 min wait (via search snippet). Shredding volume is unmeasured.
decisive_experiment: Survey 30 ITAD firms and 20 enterprises (~$50k) for the share of DIMMs destroyed; only if material, measure 24-hour remanence of 50 DDR4 and DDR5 DIMMs at 25 C.
prior_art: NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 1 volatile-memory guidance as quoted in Rohde & Schwarz security manuals (via search snippet); Halderman et al. cold-boot attacks, 2008.

key_insight: Grading retired DIMMs on retention, row-hammer threshold and speed, then binning them into CXL sleds with per-bin refresh and mitigation, makes marginal parts sellable under warranty.
killer_doubt: Retiring server DRAM is ~6-10% of bit demand; hyperscalers reuse much internally. Full hammer screening is ~2M rows per die at ~10 ms each, hours per rank; sampling must suffice.
decisive_experiment: Test 1,000 retired DDR4 RDIMMs on FPGA testers (~$300k): map retention and HCfirst per module, then show bin-tuned refresh gives zero uncorrected errors over 90 days in a CXL sled.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU; ITRenew/Sesame rack reuse; refurbished DIMM resellers; SAFARI DRAM Bender testers; stage-2 HOLD I-06172 (same mechanism).

key_insight: Periodic DRAM arrays suit self-assembly: a guided block-copolymer hex lattice at proven ~20-30 nm pitch can replace EUV hole layers in a 4F2 vertical-channel cell (Phase B N-30).
killer_doubt: At 10 nm pitch a 5 nm wire leaves ~2.5 nm per side for oxide, wordline and isolation. The node holds ~0.01 fF (~70 e-/V); ~1.5 nm LER swamps Vt.
decisive_experiment: University-fab run (~$300k): guided high-chi block-copolymer hex lattice at 10-12 nm pitch on ArF guides; measure defects over 1 cm2, CD and LER after transfer into oxide, then attempt a gate wrap.
prior_art: imec and IBM DSA contact-hole multiplication; high-chi sub-10 nm block copolymers (MIT, UT Austin); 4F2 vertical-channel DRAM (Samsung, CXMT); Phase B N-30.
